key_insight: θ-TaN shows strong directional tensile anisotropy: the c-axis is stronger and stiffer, while the a-axis is more ductile, and fracture occurs by cleavage rather than dislocation-mediated plasticity.
engineering_relevance: These atomistic strength and fracture maps help screen θ-TaN for thermally conductive interconnects and device heat-spreader applications where orientation and temperature strongly affect reliability.
method: Size, strain-rate, and temperature sensitivity checks
evidence_signal: A 20 nm model was sufficient for convergence, properties varied by less than 3.5% over 10^7 to 10^9 s^-1 strain rates, and strength remained above 73% of the 300 K value at 900 K.
watch_item: Results are based on high-rate atomistic simulations, so direct transfer to experimental loading rates and defect-rich real microstructures may require caution.
paper_title: Anisotropic Tensile Strength and Fracture Mechanism of $θ$-TaN: A Machine-Learning Potential Molecular Dynamics Study
